lead: the cabinet in her hall was ordered plain and came back plain, with the shelf set where her mother can reach it without asking, and nobody at that address has ever remarked on it.
sun: every order arrives twice. there is the one written down, a size, a wood, a date, and there is the one the customer worked around while describing it, which is the difficulty the piece will actually have to answer. you take the second one. so the object leaves your place fitted to a problem that was never stated, and it does its work in a house where nobody has agreed the problem is there.
moon: then it goes out, without a list. the making here keeps no receipt: the piece is delivered, the motion it started carries on in that house for twenty years, and no part of you stayed with it. one object ends up carrying two separate failures of record. the difficulty it answers never surfaced as anything anybody saw, and the answer left under the shop's name.
pull: the piece is in daily use and neither half of it can be shown — the difficulty it answers never became visible, and the making went out under a name that is not yours.
tension: they call you handy, fondly, and the word turns a life of exactly aimed work into a general willingness to help out. correcting it is unavailable. the accurate version starts with the afternoon you heard what she could not say about her mother, and telling her that turns a cabinet she likes into evidence that she was assessed. so handy stands, and the ones who come back for a second piece cannot say why the first suited them.
cost: the customer takes home a piece fitted to the thing they could not put into a sentence, and believes they specified it down to the shelf. nothing anywhere records either half. the objects are in use and unremarkable, the reasons for them live in one head, and the whole evidence of a thirty-year skill is a set of houses in which nothing has gone wrong.

lead: visitors get walked through it — the corridor width, the chairs, the quiet room by the door instead of at the end. one spring's work, and the only part of your working life anybody can point at.
sun: every one of those decisions came off something overheard. eleven years of hearing where the place actually hurt, which conversation had nowhere to happen, which ten minutes of the day broke people, went into a plan, and a plan is the one form that material can take without naming a single person. so the years are in the building, holding it up, and unreadable as years.
moon: and it stands there with nothing on it. no note explains why the corridor is that width, so the object shows its results and never its reasons. anyone arriving later can read it, admire it, and cut into it. the only defence available would be to repeat out loud, in a meeting, the sentences the plan was built out of.
pull: the one thing of yours anybody can see is eleven years of listening turned into a floor plan, and the floor plan cannot say a word in its own defence.
tension: the plan gets credited to an eye for space. that praises a faculty you do not have — what produced it was a decade of taking in what nobody there could afford to say out loud, and the admiration is the only return any of that has generated. arguing would mean sourcing it, and the sources are people still working in the building who would find their own worst month in a corridor.
cost: staff who have never spoken to you work inside a place fitted to complaints they never made, and they feel the fit daily without once wondering where it came from. the plan is also the whole of your record. every judgement of your working life gets taken off one artefact, in good light, with no protection on it and no account attached of how it was known.

lead: how do you two know each other, she asks, pleasantly, holding a glass — and the true answer runs through a kitchen at midnight, a bad autumn, and a sentence her friend has never said aloud to anybody placed.
sun: the intake never asked what you were to anybody. it runs in kitchens you have no business in, in waiting rooms, on people who could not say what your job is or whose side you are on, and having no place is exactly why the material arrives at full strength. somebody with a position has a route the information could travel down. you have none, so they tell you all of it.
moon: and there is nowhere for it to go afterwards. what you heard cannot be raised at a meeting you do not attend or taken to a person who would first have to ask who you are, so it converts into direct acts: an evening, a loan, a call to somebody you know from a life nobody has connected to this one. the acts work. none can be filed.
pull: people tell you everything because you are not anybody's. what you do about it happens directly, one at a time, and afterwards nobody involved can say what you were to them.
tension: the trouble arrives at the introduction. somebody has to describe you to a stranger and stalls — a friend, they settle on, or a sort of family friend — and then the stranger spends the evening working out how much you know about that household. unplaced and informed is a combination people find they do not like, and nobody has ever said so to your face. the invitations simply thin.
cost: somebody in real trouble gets your whole attention without establishing a claim on it first, which is available from almost nobody, and it works because there is no relation to damage. returning it is the part that fails. an obligation needs two placed people, and the one who owes you cannot name what you are, so it comes back as warmth from people who would not think to ring.

lead: eleven years into a boundary dispute that should have taken one. you know what the man next door is actually defending, and it has nothing to do with the fence, and you are fighting both things at once.
sun: he says it is about the drainage and the deeds, and he means it; that version is the one a solicitor can hold. underneath, audible since the first meeting, is a man whose son thinks he was a fraud and who needs one thing in his life to have been defended properly. you took delivery of that in the opening year, unasked, and it has been in the case ever since.
moon: neither of them can be set down. so you run two whole fights: the fence, argued properly, on paper, at the correct volume, and the other one, answered in moves that read as nothing on paper — an offer withdrawn, a summer let go, a concession no solicitor requested. both are carrying weight. both take their own length of time, and the second has no end date on it anywhere.
pull: your side wants you to go at the fence. for eleven years you have been fighting the thing he cannot say out loud, and winning that one is worth more and shows nothing.
tension: your own household reached a verdict years ago and delivers it kindly, with some heat behind it now: no stomach for it. that fits everything visible — the unanswered letters, the offer that went further than it had to, the summer you let the survey lapse. the accurate account requires telling your own side that you have been carrying the other man's real grievance at full weight since before any of this had a file, and no side forgives that.
cost: a fight ends here and stays ended, because what got settled was the thing actually holding it up, and nothing comes round the following year wearing a different complaint. the length is what nobody at your table forgives. eleven years reads as defeat from every seat in the room, and the half you did win happened in a man's kitchen with no witness to it and nothing on paper.
